svg.title: How a node boots: the eight-step chain this tutorial builds, and which section builds each step
svg.desc: A node's boot, from power-on to a Kubernetes cluster, in eight steps. Step one, power on and network-boot, is the only step that has to be faked on a cloud: OpenStack has no boot-from-network option, so section 9 makes iPXE the node's root disk. Steps two to six are identical to what happens on a real HPC cluster and are unmodified OpenCHAMI: CoreDHCP looks the node's MAC up in SMD and leases it the IP SMD holds (sections 7 and 8); the firmware or iPXE asks BSS for this node's boot script (section 11); it downloads the Talos kernel and initramfs from the head node's S3 store (section 10); Talos boots into RAM and enters maintenance mode (section 12); and it fetches its machine config from the talos.config URL on its kernel command line (sections 10 and 11). Steps seven and eight are Talos's own, after OpenCHAMI has handed over: Talos pulls its installer, writes itself to disk and reboots, then joins or forms a Kubernetes cluster (section 12).
svg.text: How a node boots — the chain this tutorial builds
Amber exists only because this is a cloud. Blue is unmodified OpenCHAMI, identical on real hardware. Grey is Talos's own, after OpenCHAMI hands over.
THE ONLY STEP FAKED ON A CLOUD — DECISION 2
1 · Power on → firmware network-boots
On OpenStack there is no network-boot option, so the firmware boots ipxe.usb from the node's root disk
On real hardware: a BMC's “boot from PXE, then reset”
UNMODIFIED OPENCHAMI — IDENTICAL ON A REAL HPC CLUSTER
2 · DHCP: CoreDHCP looks the MAC up in SMD, leases its IP
SMD is the single source of truth; the lease is derived from it on demand
CoreSMD — CoreDHCP with an SMD plugin
3 · The firmware / iPXE asks BSS for this node's boot script
Kernel, initramfs and kernel command line, keyed by MAC
BSS — one payload per node role
4 · Downloads the Talos kernel + initramfs from the S3 store
Prebuilt vmlinuz and initramfs.xz — no image build at all
Versity S3 gateway on the head node
5 · Talos boots into RAM, enters maintenance mode
No shell and no SSH — from here on, talosctl is the only way in
Waiting for a machine config
6 · Fetches its machine config from the talos.config URL
The URL arrives as a kernel argument, which is BSS's job — Talos ignores cloud-init
A declarative config, one per role
TALOS'S OWN — OPENCHAMI HAS HANDED OVER
7 · Pulls its installer, writes itself to disk, reboots
Overwrites the iPXE bootloader, so the next boot is Talos from disk — nothing remembers which nodes are done
Needs the internet, through the head's NAT (§7.12)
8 · Joins / forms a Kubernetes cluster
The control-plane node bootstraps etcd; the workers join it
Then §§13–18 build the inference stack on top
Steps 2 to 6 are the same on real metal. Only step 1 changes, and on real hardware it is one Redfish call.
